data.cultural_impact: The name "शुभम् (Śubham)" holds cultural significance in Hinduism and other Indian traditions. It is often used as a salutation or a way to express good wishes and blessings towards others. For instance, in traditional Indian customs, guests are welcomed by saying "शुभ मासावे" (śubh māsāvē), which means "May this month bring happiness to you" or "शुभ रात्रि" (śubh rātri), which means " Auspicious night". Furthermore, it is often used as a title before the name of a revered person to signify respect and honor.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "शुभम् (Śubham)" carries deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. It is believed that using the name as a form of blessing or wishing good fortune upon someone invokes the blessings of the Hindu gods. The name acts as a reminder to always strive for positivity, happiness, and good fortune in life. Additionally, it is considered a form of manifesting positivity and good energy into the world. By using the name, one is literally invoking the essence of auspiciousness and blessings into their own being and that of others.

historical_references.reference: The name 'शुभम' is mentioned in the ancient Indian scripture, the Rigveda, which is one of the oldest known scriptures in the world, originating from around 1500 BCE. The name is used in various hymns as an expression of good fortune and prosperity.

'शुभम' is also used in Hindu religious texts like the Mahabharata, which was composed between 400 BCE and 200 CE. In this epic, 'शुभम' is often used as a name of the god Shiva, representing auspiciousness and godliness.
